newsitem.title: RUSSIA: DMG rules out early sale of Svyazinvest stake.
newsitem.headline: DMG rules out early sale of Svyazinvest stake.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), the investment banking division of Germany's Deutsche Bank, said on Tuesday it does not plan an early sale of the stake it won in Russian telecoms holding company Svyazinvest.
DMG is a member of the Mustcom financial consortium which last Friday won a 25 percent plus one share stake in Svyazinvest for $1.875 billion, in Russia's biggest privatisation to date.

DMG's managing director in Moscow, Nick Jordan, told Reuters the consortium's strategy was being managed by Vladimir Potanin, the 36-year-old president of Russia's Uneximbank, but he said he thought none of the members planned to sell out soon.
"I don't believe that anyone sees this as a flip," he said.

Jordan also dismissed speculation that the consortium could split the stake, with, for example, Uneximbank holding on to part of Svyazinvest, and DMG and other partners selling out to other investors.
"The agreement is that the investors are in it together," he said.

Billionaire financier George Soros, whose Quantum fund is also part of the consortium, was quoted on Tuesday by the London business daily Financial Times as saying he had invested $980 million in Svyazinvest.
Potanin, who had a brief tenure as first deputy prime minister until March, will sign the contract with the government on behalf of the consortium on Thursday, a Potanin aide said.
She added the bank, Russia's third largest, was going to investigate the possibility of bidding for a further 24 percent stake in Svayzinvest, to be offered to Russian investors this year or next.
